  mockClient.comparison = {
    findFirst: async (args: any) => {
      const slug = args?.where?.slug;
      const comp = allComparisons.find((c) => c.slug === slug);
      if (!comp) return null;
      return buildComparisonObject(comp);
    },
    findMany: async (args?: any) => {
      let matches = [...allComparisons];

      // where: { published }
      if (args?.where?.published !== undefined) {
        matches = matches.filter((c) => c.published === args.where.published);
      }

      // orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" | "asc" } — mock data has no real
      // createdAt, so this is a stable no-op ordering (reversed for asc)
      if (args?.orderBy?.createdAt === "asc") {
        matches = matches.slice().reverse();
      }

      // take / skip
      if (args?.skip) matches = matches.slice(args.skip);
      if (args?.take) matches = matches.slice(0, args.take);

      const include = args?.include || {};
      const select = args?.select;

      return matches.map((c) => {
        // If a `select` is provided, honor it (compare/browse pages).
        if (select) {
          const base = {
            id: `comp_${c.slug}`,
            title: c.title,
            slug: c.slug,
            summary: c.summary,
            published: c.published,
            platformAId: c.platformA,
            platformBId: c.platformB,
            createdAt: new Date(),
          };
          const picked: any = {};
          for (const key of Object.keys(select)) {
            if (select[key] && key in base) {
              picked[key] = (base as any)[key];
            }
          }
          // Nested include inside select (rare) — fall back to full
          if (select.platformA || select.platformB) {
            const full = buildComparisonObject(c);
            return {
              ...picked,
              ...(select.platformA ? { platformA: full.platformA } : {}),
              ...(select.platformB ? { platformB: full.platformB } : {}),
            };
          }
          return picked;
        }

        // No select — build the base row, then attach includes
        const row: any = {
          id: `comp_${c.slug}`,
          title: c.title,
          slug: c.slug,
          summary: c.summary,
          published: c.published,
          platformAId: c.platformA,
          platformBId: c.platformB,
          createdAt: new Date(),
        };

        if (include.platformA || include.platformB) {
          const full = buildComparisonObject(c);
          if (include.platformA) row.platformA = full.platformA;
          if (include.platformB) row.platformB = full.platformB;
        }
        if (include.facts) {
          row.facts = c.facts.map((f, i) => ({
            id: `fact_${i}`,
            title: f.title,
            platformAValue: f.platformAValue,
            platformBValue: f.platformBValue,
          }));
        }
        if (include.faqs) {
          row.faqs = (c.faqs || []).map((f, i) => ({
            id: `faq_${i}`,
            question: f.question,
            answer: f.answer,
          }));
        }
        return row;
      });
    },
    findUnique: async (args: any) => {
      const slug = args?.where?.slug;
      const id = args?.where?.id;
      const comp = allComparisons.find(
        (c) => c.slug === slug || `comp_${c.slug}` === id,
      );
      if (!comp) return null;
      return buildComparisonObject(comp);
    },
    count: async (args?: any) => {
      let matches = [...allComparisons];
      if (args?.where?.published !== undefined) {
        matches = matches.filter((c) => c.published === args.where.published);
      }
      return matches.length;
    },
    create: async (args: any) => ({
      id: `comp_new_${Date.now()}`,
      ...args?.data,
    }),
    update: async (args: any) => ({ id: args?.where?.id, ...args?.data }),
    upsert: async (args: any) => ({
      id: args?.where?.slug || `comp_${Date.now()}`,
      ...args?.create,
      ...args?.update,
    }),
    delete: async () => ({}),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  mockClient.feature = {
    findMany: async () => {
      const uniqueFeatures = new Set<string>();
      allPlatforms.forEach((p) => {
        p.features.forEach((f) => uniqueFeatures.add(f.featureName));
      });

      return Array.from(uniqueFeatures).map((featName, i) => {
        // Find category name from any platform that has this feature
        let catName = "Features";
        for (const p of allPlatforms) {
          const match = p.features.find((f) => f.featureName === featName);
          if (match) {
            catName = match.categoryName;
            break;
          }
        }

        return {
          id: featName,
          name: featName,
          categoryId: catName,
          category: {
            id: catName,
            name: catName
          }
        };
      });
    },
    findUnique: async (args: any) => {
      const name = args?.where?.name || args?.where?.id;
      for (const p of allPlatforms) {
        const match = p.features.find((f) => f.featureName === name);
        if (match) return { id: name, name, categoryId: match.categoryName, category: { id: match.categoryName, name: match.categoryName } };
      }
      return null;
    },
    findFirst: async (args: any) => {
      const name = args?.where?.name;
      for (const p of allPlatforms) {
        const match = p.features.find((f) => f.featureName === name);
        if (match) return { id: name, name, categoryId: match.categoryName, category: { id: match.categoryName, name: match.categoryName } };
      }
      return null;
    },
    count: async () => {
      const uniqueFeatures = new Set<string>();
      allPlatforms.forEach((p) => p.features.forEach((f) => uniqueFeatures.add(f.featureName)));
      return uniqueFeatures.size;
    },
    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `feat_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data }),
    upsert: async (args: any) => ({ id: args?.where?.name || `feat_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.create, ...args?.update }),

  mockClient.post = {
    findMany: async (args?: any) => {
      let results = [...mockPostItems];
      if (args?.where?.published !== undefined) results = results.filter((r) => r.published === args.where.published);
      if (args?.where?.authorId) results = results.filter((r) => r.authorId === args.where.authorId);
      if (args?.where?.categoryId) results = results.filter((r) => r.categoryId === args.where.categoryId);
      if (args?.where?.id?.not) results = results.filter((r) => r.id !== args.where.id.not);
      if (args?.where?.OR) {
        const orFilters = args.where.OR;
        results = results.filter((r) => {
          return orFilters.some((filter: any) => {
            if (filter.title?.contains) return r.title.toLowerCase().includes(filter.title.contains.toLowerCase());
            if (filter.description?.contains) return r.description.toLowerCase().includes(filter.description.contains.toLowerCase());
            if (filter.content?.contains) return r.content.toLowerCase().includes(filter.content.contains.toLowerCase());
            return false;
          });
        });
      }
      if (args?.orderBy) {
        const key = Object.keys(args.orderBy)[0];
        const dir = args.orderBy[key];
        results.sort((a: any, b: any) => {
          const aVal = a[key];
          const bVal = b[key];
          if (aVal instanceof Date && bVal instanceof Date) {
            return dir === "asc" ? aVal.getTime() - bVal.getTime() : bVal.getTime() - aVal.getTime();
          }
          return dir === "asc" ? String(aVal).localeCompare(String(bVal)) : String(bVal).localeCompare(String(aVal));
        });
      }
      if (args?.take) results = results.slice(0, args.take);
      // Strip heavy fields if only selecting specific fields
      if (args?.select) {
        return results.map((r) => {
          const selected: any = {};
          for (const key of Object.keys(args.select)) {
            selected[key] = (r as any)[key];
          }
          return selected;
        });
      }
      return results;
    },
    findFirst: async (args: any) => {
      const slug = args?.where?.slug;
      const id = args?.where?.id;
      let found = mockPostItems.find((p) => p.slug === slug || p.id === id);
      if (!found && args?.where?.slug) found = mockPostItems.find((p) => p.slug === args.where.slug);
      return found || null;
    },
    findUnique: async (args: any) => {
      const slug = args?.where?.slug;
      const id = args?.where?.id;
      return mockPostItems.find((p) => p.slug === slug || p.id === id) || null;
    },
    count: async () => mockPostItems.length,
    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `post_new_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data, createdAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() }),
    update: async (args: any) => ({ id: args?.where?.id, ...args?.data, updatedAt: new Date() }),
    upsert: async (args: any) => ({ id: args?.where?.slug || `post_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.create, ...args?.update }),
    delete: async () => ({}),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  mockClient.platform = {
    findUnique: async (args: any) => {
      const name = args?.where?.name || args?.where?.id;
      const plat = allPlatforms.find((p) => p.name === name || p.name.toLowerCase() === String(name).toLowerCase());
      if (!plat) return null;
      return {
        id: `plat_${plat.name.toLowerCase()}`,
        ...plat,
      };
    },
    findFirst: async (args: any) => {
      const name = args?.where?.name;
      // Support insensitive search via OR array
      if (args?.where?.OR) {
        for (const condition of args.where.OR) {
          if (condition.name?.equals) {
            const found = allPlatforms.find((p) => p.name.toLowerCase() === condition.name.equals.toLowerCase());
            if (found) return { id: `plat_${found.name.toLowerCase()}`, ...found };
          }
          if (condition.id) {
            const found = allPlatforms.find((p) => `plat_${p.name.toLowerCase()}` === condition.id || p.name.toLowerCase() === condition.id.toLowerCase());
            if (found) return { id: `plat_${found.name.toLowerCase()}`, ...found };
          }
        }
        return null;
      }
      const plat = allPlatforms.find((p) => p.name === name || p.name.toLowerCase() === String(name || "").toLowerCase());
      if (!plat) return null;
      return {
        id: `plat_${plat.name.toLowerCase()}`,
        ...plat,
      };
    },
    findMany: async (args?: any) => {
      let results = allPlatforms.map((plat) => ({
        id: `plat_${plat.name.toLowerCase()}`,
        ...plat,
      }));
      if (args?.where?.name?.in) {
        results = results.filter((p) => args.where.name.in.includes(p.name));
      }
      if (args?.select) {
        return results.map((r) => {
          const selected: any = {};
          for (const key of Object.keys(args.select)) {
            selected[key] = (r as any)[key];
          }
          return selected;
        });
      }
      return results;
    },
    count: async () => allPlatforms.length,
    create: async (args: any) => ({
      id: `plat_${args?.data?.name?.toLowerCase() || 'unknown'}`,
      ...args?.data,
    }),
    update: async (args: any) => ({
      id: args?.where?.id || 'unknown',
      ...args?.data,
    }),
    upsert: async (args: any) => ({
      id: `plat_${args?.create?.name?.toLowerCase() || 'unknown'}`,
      ...args?.create,
    }),
  };

    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `pf_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data }),
    update: async (args: any) => ({ id: args?.where?.id, ...args?.data }),
    upsert: async (args: any) => ({ id: `pf_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.create, ...args?.update }),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  mockClient.pricingTier = {
    findMany: async () => [],
    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `tier_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data }),
    createMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // FACT / FAQ — stand-alone models
  // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  mockClient.fact = {
    findMany: async () => [],
    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `fact_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data }),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  mockClient.faq = {
    findMany: async () => [],
    create: async (args: any) => ({ id: `faq_${Date.now()}`, ...args?.data }),
    deleteMany: async () => ({ count: 0 }),
  };

  // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Add standard Prisma methods
  // ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  mockClient.$disconnect = async () => {};
  mockClient.$connect = async () => {};

  // Return a proxy that dynamically handles any model accessor to prevent crashes
  return new Proxy(mockClient, {
    get(target, prop) {
      const propStr = String(prop);
      if (propStr === '$disconnect' || propStr === '$connect') {
        return async () => {};
      }
      if (propStr.startsWith('$')) {
        return async (...args: any[]) => {
          console.log(`[Mock Prisma] Intercepted client method: ${propStr}`);
          if (propStr === '$transaction' && typeof args[0] === 'function') {
            return await args[0](target);
          }
          if (propStr === '$transaction' && Array.isArray(args[0])) {
            return await Promise.all(args[0]);
          }
          return {};
        };
      }

      if (mockClient[propStr]) {
        return mockClient[propStr];
      }

      // Fallback model proxy for any other model not explicitly mocked
      return new Proxy({}, {
        get(modelTarget, method) {
          return async () => {
            console.log(`[Mock Prisma Fallback] Intercepted ${propStr}.${String(method)}`);
            if (String(method) === 'findMany') return [];
            if (String(method) === 'count') return 0;
            if (String(method) === 'deleteMany') return { count: 0 };
            if (String(method) === 'updateMany') return { count: 0 };
            if (String(method) === 'createMany') return { count: 0 };
            return null;
          };
        }
      });
    }
  });
};

const getPrismaClient = () => {
  const connectionString = process.env.DATABASE_URL;
  const isSeeding = process.argv.some(arg => arg.includes('seed')) || process.env.npm_lifecycle_event?.includes('seed');
  const bypassMock = process.env.MOCK_PRISMA === "false" || process.env.BYPASS_MOCK === "true" || isSeeding;

  // Use the Mock Prisma Client if:
  // 1. BYPASS_MOCK is not "true" (default: use mock)
  // 2. DATABASE_URL is missing, dummy, or localhost
  // 3. BUILD_TYPE is "static"
  if (
    !connectionString ||
    (!bypassMock && (connectionString.includes("localhost") || connectionString.includes("127.0.0.1"))) ||
    connectionString.includes("example.com") ||
    process.env.BUILD_TYPE === "static" ||
    (!bypassMock && !connectionString)
  ) {
    return createMockPrismaClient();
  }

  // If bypassMock is false and we have a real connection string,
  // still use mock (user wants zero-database mode)
  if (!bypassMock) {
    return createMockPrismaClient();
  }

  try {
    return new PrismaClient({
      log: ["error"],
    });
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("❌ Failed to initialize live Prisma Client, falling back to mock:", error);
    return createMockPrismaClient();
  }
};

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as {
  prismaGlobal: any | undefined;
};

export const prisma = globalForPrisma.prismaGlobal ?? getPrismaClient();

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") {
  globalForPrisma.prismaGlobal = prisma;
}

export default prisma as PrismaClient;

export interface PricingTier {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  monthlyPrice: number;
  annualPriceMonthlyEquivalent: number | null;
  transactionFeePercent: number | null;
}

export interface Platform {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  tiers: PricingTier[];
}

export interface GatewayConfig {
  name: string;
  percent: number;
  fixed: number;
}

export const GATEWAYS: Record<string, GatewayConfig> = {
  stripe: { name: "Stripe", percent: 2.9, fixed: 0.30 },
  paypal: { name: "PayPal", percent: 3.49, fixed: 0.49 },
  none: { name: "No Fees / Custom", percent: 0, fixed: 0 },
};

export interface WealthForecast {
  year: number;
  revenue: number;
  platformFees: number;
  gatewayFees: number;
  totalCost: number;
  cumulativeCost: number;
}

export interface ROICalculationResult {
  monthlyPlatformCost: number;
  monthlyGatewayFees: number;
  monthlyTotalCost: number;
  annualTotalCost: number;
  threeYearTotalCost: number;
  fiveYearWealthLoss: number; // Cumulative cost over 5 years with growth
  breakEvenSales: number;
  effectiveFeePercent: number;
  forecast: WealthForecast[];
}

/**
 * Industrial ROI Engine with Wealth Loss Forecasting
 * Simulates growth to show the long-term impact of platform fees.
 */
export function calculateROI(
  revenue: number,
  salesCount: number,
  tier: PricingTier,
  gateway: GatewayConfig,
  billingInterval: "monthly" | "annually" = "monthly",
  annualGrowthRate: number = 0.20 // Default 20% annual growth
): ROICalculationResult {
  const platformMonthlyPrice = billingInterval === "annually" && tier.annualPriceMonthlyEquivalent !== null
    ? tier.annualPriceMonthlyEquivalent
    : tier.monthlyPrice;

  // Monthly breakdown for Year 1
  const platformTransactionFees = (revenue * (tier.transactionFeePercent || 0)) / 100;
  const monthlyPlatformCost = platformMonthlyPrice + platformTransactionFees;
  const gatewayPercentFee = (revenue * gateway.percent) / 100;
  const gatewayFixedFeeTotal = salesCount * gateway.fixed;
  const monthlyGatewayFees = gatewayPercentFee + gatewayFixedFeeTotal;
  const monthlyTotalCost = monthlyPlatformCost + monthlyGatewayFees;

  // 5-Year Forecast Logic
  const forecast: WealthForecast[] = [];
  let cumulativeCost = 0;
  let currentRevenue = revenue * 12;
  let currentSales = salesCount * 12;

  for (let year = 1; year <= 5; year++) {
    const yearPlatformFees = (platformMonthlyPrice * 12) + (currentRevenue * (tier.transactionFeePercent || 0)) / 100;
    const yearGatewayFees = (currentRevenue * gateway.percent / 100) + (currentSales * gateway.fixed);
    const yearTotalCost = yearPlatformFees + yearGatewayFees;

    cumulativeCost += yearTotalCost;

    forecast.push({
      year,
      revenue: currentRevenue,
      platformFees: yearPlatformFees,
      gatewayFees: yearGatewayFees,
      totalCost: yearTotalCost,
      cumulativeCost
    });

    // Project growth for next year
    currentRevenue *= (1 + annualGrowthRate);
    currentSales *= (1 + annualGrowthRate);
  }

  const annualTotalCost = monthlyTotalCost * 12;
  const avgPricePerSale = salesCount > 0 ? revenue / salesCount : 0;
  const variableCostPerSale = (avgPricePerSale * (gateway.percent + (tier.transactionFeePercent || 0))) / 100 + gateway.fixed;
  const marginPerSale = avgPricePerSale - variableCostPerSale;
  const breakEvenSales = marginPerSale > 0 ? Math.ceil(platformMonthlyPrice / marginPerSale) : 0;
  const effectiveFeePercent = revenue > 0 ? (monthlyTotalCost / revenue) * 100 : 0;

  return {
    monthlyPlatformCost,
    monthlyGatewayFees,
    monthlyTotalCost,
    annualTotalCost,
    threeYearTotalCost: forecast[2].cumulativeCost,
    fiveYearWealthLoss: cumulativeCost,
    breakEvenSales,
    effectiveFeePercent,
    forecast
  };
}

export interface Recommendation {
  bestTier: PricingTier;
  bestPlatform: Platform;
  annualSavings: number;
  fiveYearSavings: number;
  percentSavings: number;
}

export function findBestDeal(
  currentRevenue: number,
  currentSalesCount: number,
  currentTier: PricingTier,
  allPlatforms: Platform[],
  gateway: GatewayConfig,
  billingInterval: "monthly" | "annually" = "monthly"
): Recommendation | null {
  const currentStats = calculateROI(currentRevenue, currentSalesCount, currentTier, gateway, billingInterval);
  
  let bestRec: Recommendation | null = null;
  let maxFiveYearSavings = 0;

  for (const platform of allPlatforms) {
    for (const tier of platform.tiers) {
      if (tier.id === currentTier.id) continue;
      
      const stats = calculateROI(currentRevenue, currentSalesCount, tier, gateway, billingInterval);
      const savings = currentStats.fiveYearWealthLoss - stats.fiveYearWealthLoss;
      
      if (savings > maxFiveYearSavings) {
        maxFiveYearSavings = savings;
        bestRec = {
          bestTier: tier,
          bestPlatform: platform,
          annualSavings: currentStats.annualTotalCost - stats.annualTotalCost,
          fiveYearSavings: savings,
          percentSavings: (savings / currentStats.fiveYearWealthLoss) * 100
        };
      }
    }
  }

  return bestRec;
}

import { PlatformData } from "@/data/compare/types";

export type VerificationConfidence = "HIGH" | "MODERATE" | "BASIC";

export interface ScorePillar {
  name: string;
  key: "features" | "value" | "sovereignty" | "ux" | "integrations";
  score: number; // 0 to 5 scale
  weight: number; // Percentage float (0.30, 0.25, etc)
  weightLabel: string; // e.g., "30%"
  description: string;
  evidence: string; // "Why this score?" structured explanation
  dataPointsCount: number;
}

export interface CreatorFitScore {
  type: "course" | "newsletter" | "community" | "solopreneur" | "enterprise";
  label: string;
  score: number; // 0-100
  description: string;
}

export interface ScoreDeltaReason {
  date: string;
  changeAmount: number; // e.g., +4
  summary: string;
  affectedPillars: { pillarName: string; delta: number }[];
}

export interface VerificationEvidence {
  confidence: VerificationConfidence;
  confidenceScore: number; // 0-100
  reasons: string[];
  sources: { title: string; url: string }[];
  lastVerifiedDaysAgo: number;
}

export interface PlatformScorecard {
  overallScore: number; // 0 to 100
  grade: "S" | "A+" | "A" | "B+" | "B" | "C";
  verdict: string;
  confidence: VerificationConfidence;
  evidenceDetails: VerificationEvidence;
  pillars: ScorePillar[];
  whyChoose: string[]; // "Why X?" key strengths
  whyNotChoose: string[]; // "Why NOT X?" key limitations
  creatorFits: CreatorFitScore[];
  scoreTrend?: {
    change6Months: number; // e.g. +4 or -2
    deltaExplanation: ScoreDeltaReason;
    previousScores: { date: string; score: number }[];
  };
}

export interface UserPillarWeights {
  featuresWeight: number; // e.g., 0-100 scale slider
  valueWeight: number;
  sovereigntyWeight: number;
  uxWeight: number;
  integrationsWeight: number;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*                             SAFETY HELPERS                                 */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/**
 * Returns the first finite number from candidates, otherwise the fallback.
 * Safely ignores null, undefined, NaN, Infinity, and non-number types.
 */
function firstFiniteNumber(
  fallback: number,
  ...candidates: Array<number | null | undefined | unknown>
): number {
  for (const c of candidates) {
    if (typeof c === "number" && Number.isFinite(c)) {
      return c;
    }
  }
  return fallback;
}

/**
 * Safe wrapper: coerces a possibly-null/undefined value into a finite number.
 */
function safeNumber(value: unknown, fallback: number): number {
  return typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value) ? value : fallback;
}

/**
 * Safe rounding for display: guarantees a valid number before calling toFixed.
 */
function roundTo1(value: number): number {
  const safe = Number.isFinite(value) ? value : 0;
  return Number(safe.toFixed(1));
}

/**
 * Parses a date value, returning a valid Date or the provided fallback.
 */
function safeDate(value: unknown, fallback: Date): Date {
  if (!value) return fallback;
  const d = new Date(value as string | number | Date);
  return Number.isNaN(d.getTime()) ? fallback : d;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*                        PLATFORM SCORECARD CALCULATOR                       */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/**
 * Computes the transparent 5-pillar Comparlify Creator Intelligence Scorecard.
 * Weight Distribution:
 * - Features: 30%
 * - Value & Pricing: 25%
 * - Data & Code Sovereignty: 15%
 * - Ease of Use & UX: 15%
 * - Ecosystem & Integrations: 15%
 */
export function calculatePlatformScore(
  platform: Partial<PlatformData> & { name: string }
): PlatformScorecard {
  // Guard against completely missing platform object
  const safePlatform = platform ?? ({ name: "Unknown Platform" } as Partial<PlatformData> & { name: string });

  /* ----------------------- Resolve pillar scores safely ---------------------- */

  const featuresScore = firstFiniteNumber(
    4.5,
    safePlatform.featuresRating,
    safePlatform.rating
  );

  const valueScore = firstFiniteNumber(4.3, safePlatform.valueRating);

  // Sovereignty: handle null, undefined, and out-of-range numbers.
  // Accepts either 0-5 (sovereigntyRating) or 0-100 (sovereigntyScore / audit.sovereigntyScore).
  let sovereigntyScore = 4.2;

  const rawSovRating = safePlatform.sovereigntyRating;
  const rawSovScore = safePlatform.sovereigntyScore;
  const rawAuditSov = safePlatform.audit?.sovereigntyScore;

  if (typeof rawSovRating === "number" && Number.isFinite(rawSovRating)) {
    sovereigntyScore = rawSovRating;
  } else if (typeof rawSovScore === "number" && Number.isFinite(rawSovScore)) {
    sovereigntyScore = rawSovScore / 20;
  } else if (typeof rawAuditSov === "number" && Number.isFinite(rawAuditSov)) {
    sovereigntyScore = rawAuditSov / 20;
  }

  // Clamp sovereignty to 0-5 to prevent inflated weighting
  sovereigntyScore = Math.min(5, Math.max(0, sovereigntyScore));

  const uxScore = firstFiniteNumber(4.3, safePlatform.easeOfUse);
  const integrationsScore = firstFiniteNumber(4.4, safePlatform.integrationsRating);

  /* --------------------------- Weighted overall score ------------------------ */

  const weightedSum =
    featuresScore * 0.30 +
    valueScore * 0.25 +
    sovereigntyScore * 0.15 +
    uxScore * 0.15 +
    integrationsScore * 0.15;

  const overallScore = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.max(0, Math.round(safeNumber(weightedSum * 20, 0)))
  );

  /* ------------------------------- Grade verdict ----------------------------- */

  let grade: PlatformScorecard["grade"] = "B";
  let verdict = "Solid choice with standard features and baseline value.";

  if (overallScore >= 95) {
    grade = "S";
    verdict = "Industry-defining platform excellence. Top score across sovereignty, features, and scale value.";
  } else if (overallScore >= 90) {
    grade = "A+";
    verdict = "Tier-1 enterprise infrastructure. Outstanding value, performance, and creator sovereignty.";
  } else if (overallScore >= 84) {
    grade = "A";
    verdict = "High-performance platform with strong core capabilities and competitive pricing.";
  } else if (overallScore >= 78) {
    grade = "B+";
    verdict = "Good option for standard workloads, though minor trade-offs exist in fees or lock-in.";
  }

  /* --------------------------- Confidence calculation ------------------------ */

  const lastVerifiedDate = safeDate(safePlatform.lastVerifiedAt, new Date("2026-03-01"));
  const now = new Date();
  const daysAgo = Math.max(
    0,
    Math.floor((now.getTime() - lastVerifiedDate.getTime()) / (1000 * 3600 * 24))
  );

  const featureItemsCount = Array.isArray(safePlatform.features)
    ? safePlatform.features.length
    : 8;
  const tiersCount = Array.isArray(safePlatform.tiers) ? safePlatform.tiers.length : 2;
  const changeLogsCount = Array.isArray((safePlatform as any).changeLogs)
    ? (safePlatform as any).changeLogs.length
    : 0;

  let confidence: VerificationConfidence = "BASIC";
  let confidenceScore = 60;
  const confidenceReasons: string[] = [];

  if (daysAgo <= 90) {
    confidenceScore += 15;
    confidenceReasons.push("Pricing & parameters verified within last 90 days");
  } else {
    confidenceReasons.push(
      "Verification date >90 days ago; automated re-audit recommended"
    );
  }

  if (featureItemsCount >= 4 && tiersCount >= 1) {
    confidenceScore += 15;
    confidenceReasons.push(
      `High data density (${featureItemsCount} feature points, ${tiersCount} pricing tiers verified)`
    );
  } else {
    confidenceReasons.push("Limited feature data points available");
  }

  if (changeLogsCount >= 1) {
    confidenceScore += 10;
    confidenceReasons.push(
      `Audited change history available (${changeLogsCount} recent updates logged)`
    );
  }

  if (safePlatform.sourceUrl) {
    confidenceScore += 5;
    confidenceReasons.push("Direct official source documentation linked");
  }

  if (confidenceScore >= 85) {
    confidence = "HIGH";
  } else if (confidenceScore >= 70) {
    confidence = "MODERATE";
  } else {
    confidence = "BASIC";
  }

  const evidenceDetails: VerificationEvidence = {
    confidence,
    confidenceScore,
    reasons: confidenceReasons,
    sources: [
      {
        title: `${safePlatform.name || "Platform"} Official Documentation & Pricing`,
        url:
          safePlatform.sourceUrl ||
          safePlatform.website ||
          "https://comparlify.com",
      },
    ],
    lastVerifiedDaysAgo: daysAgo,
  };

  /* ------------------------------- Pillar list ------------------------------- */

  const pillars: ScorePillar[] = [
    {
      name: "Core Features & Depth",
      key: "features",
      score: roundTo1(featuresScore),
      weight: 0.30,
      weightLabel: "30%",
      description:
        "Functionality, automation rules, native capabilities, and reliability.",
      dataPointsCount: Math.max(6, featureItemsCount),
      evidence:
        featuresScore >= 4.5
          ? "Robust native tooling, powerful workflow automation, and high feature density."
          : "Standard core features available, though specialized niche tools may require add-ons.",
    },
    {
      name: "Value & Margin ROI",
      key: "value",
      score: roundTo1(valueScore),
      weight: 0.25,
      weightLabel: "25%",
      description:
        "Pricing predictability, transaction fees, and revenue retention.",
      dataPointsCount: Math.max(4, tiersCount * 2),
      evidence:
        valueScore >= 4.5
          ? "0% transaction fees or flat predictable monthly tiers maximize creator margin retention."
          : "Subscription pricing scales with audience size; take-rate fees apply on lower plans.",
    },
    {
      name: "Data & Code Sovereignty",
      key: "sovereignty",
      score: roundTo1(sovereigntyScore),
      weight: 0.15,
      weightLabel: "15%",
      description:
        "Database exportability, self-hosting ability, and lock-in risk.",
      dataPointsCount: 4,
      evidence:
        sovereigntyScore >= 4.5
          ? "Full database exportability (CSV/JSON), open-source core, or complete custom domain ownership."
          : "Hosted platform lock-in; subscriber exports available but theme/code migration requires rebuild.",
    },
    {
      name: "Ease of Use & UX",
      key: "ux",
      score: roundTo1(uxScore),
      weight: 0.15,
      weightLabel: "15%",
      description: "Dashboard speed, onboarding friction, and workflow elegance.",
      dataPointsCount: 5,
      evidence:
        uxScore >= 4.5
          ? "Sub-second dashboard response, minimal onboarding curve, and intuitive publication editor."
          : "Feature-rich interface requiring moderate learning curve for new creators.",
    },
    {
      name: "Ecosystem & Integrations",
      key: "integrations",
      score: roundTo1(integrationsScore),
      weight: 0.15,
      weightLabel: "15%",
      description:
        "API flexibility, webhooks, app marketplace, and third-party tools.",
      dataPointsCount: 5,
      evidence:
        integrationsScore >= 4.5
          ? "Extensive Zapier/Make webhooks, open REST APIs, and active developer ecosystem."
          : "Essential webhooks supported; REST API access limited to higher tier plans.",
    },
  ];

  /* ----------------------------- Why / Why Not ------------------------------ */

  const platformPros = Array.isArray(safePlatform.pros)
    ? (safePlatform.pros as string[])
    : [];
  const platformCons = Array.isArray(safePlatform.cons)
    ? (safePlatform.cons as string[])
    : [];

  const whyChoose =
    platformPros.slice(0, 3).length > 0
      ? platformPros.slice(0, 3)
      : [
          "High core reliability & performance",
          "Predictable feature architecture",
          "Clean user experience",
        ];

  const whyNotChoose =
    platformCons.slice(0, 3).length > 0
      ? platformCons.slice(0, 3)
      : [
          "Higher scaling cost at high subscriber volume",
          "Moderate setup learning curve",
          "Niche feature restrictions",
        ];

  /* ------------------------------ Creator fits ------------------------------ */

  const courseFit = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.round((featuresScore * 0.4 + uxScore * 0.3 + valueScore * 0.3) * 20)
  );
  const newsletterFit = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.round(
      (sovereigntyScore * 0.35 + valueScore * 0.35 + uxScore * 0.3) * 20
    )
  );
  const communityFit = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.round(
      (featuresScore * 0.35 + integrationsScore * 0.35 + uxScore * 0.3) * 20
    )
  );
  const solopreneurFit = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.round((uxScore * 0.4 + valueScore * 0.4 + featuresScore * 0.2) * 20)
  );
  const enterpriseFit = Math.min(
    100,
    Math.round(
      (featuresScore * 0.35 + sovereigntyScore * 0.35 + integrationsScore * 0.3) *
        20
    )
  );

  const creatorFits: CreatorFitScore[] = [
    {
      type: "course",
      label: "Course Creators",
      score: courseFit,
      description: "Structured video hosting, quizzes, & drip content.",
    },
    {
      type: "newsletter",
      label: "Newsletter Writers",
      score: newsletterFit,
      description: "High deliverability, subscription tiers, & SEO.",
    },
    {
      type: "community",
      label: "Community Builders",
      score: communityFit,
      description: "Gamified feeds, group spaces, & event management.",
    },
    {
      type: "solopreneur",
      label: "Lean Solopreneurs",
      score: solopreneurFit,
      description: "Low operational overhead & fast launch velocity.",
    },
    {
      type: "enterprise",
      label: "Enterprise Studios",
      score: enterpriseFit,
      description: "Custom SSO, API access, & multi-admin roles.",
    },
  ];

  /* ------------------------------ Score trend ------------------------------- */

  const changeLogsList = Array.isArray((safePlatform as any).changeLogs)
    ? (safePlatform as any).changeLogs
    : [];
  const latestLog = changeLogsList.length > 0 ? changeLogsList[0] : null;

  const deltaSummary = latestLog
    ? `Score updated: ${latestLog.title ?? "Audit"}. ${latestLog.description ?? ""}`
    : `Stable platform parameters confirmed under ${lastVerifiedDate.getFullYear()} audit.`;

  const deltaDate = latestLog?.date
    ? safeDate(latestLog.date, new Date()).toLocaleDateString("en-US", {
        month: "short",
        year: "numeric",
      })
    : "Recent Audit";

  return {
    overallScore,
    grade,
    verdict,
    confidence,
    evidenceDetails,
    pillars,
    whyChoose,
    whyNotChoose,
    creatorFits,
    scoreTrend: {
      change6Months: latestLog ? 3 : 0,
      deltaExplanation: {
        date: deltaDate,
        changeAmount: latestLog ? 3 : 0,
        summary: deltaSummary,
        affectedPillars: [
          { pillarName: "Features & Depth", delta: 2 },
          { pillarName: "Value & Pricing ROI", delta: 1 },
        ],
      },
      previousScores: [
        { date: "2026-03", score: overallScore },
        { date: "2026-01", score: Math.max(70, overallScore - 2) },
        { date: "2025-10", score: Math.max(70, overallScore - 4) },
      ],
    },
  };
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
/*                    PERSONALIZED MATCH SCORE CALCULATOR                     */
/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------- */

/**
 * Calculates personalized match score based on individual creator weight preferences.
 */
export function calculatePersonalMatchScore(
  platform: Partial<PlatformData> & { name: string },
  userWeights: UserPillarWeights
): number {
  const scorecard = calculatePlatformScore(platform);

  const safeWeights: UserPillarWeights = {
    featuresWeight: safeNumber(userWeights?.featuresWeight, 0),
    valueWeight: safeNumber(userWeights?.valueWeight, 0),
    sovereigntyWeight: safeNumber(userWeights?.sovereigntyWeight, 0),
    uxWeight: safeNumber(userWeights?.uxWeight, 0),
    integrationsWeight: safeNumber(userWeights?.integrationsWeight, 0),
  };

  const totalWeight =
    safeWeights.featuresWeight +
    safeWeights.valueWeight +
    safeWeights.sovereigntyWeight +
    safeWeights.uxWeight +
    safeWeights.integrationsWeight;

  if (totalWeight === 0) return scorecard.overallScore;

  const featuresPillar =
    scorecard.pillars.find((p) => p.key === "features")?.score ?? 4;
  const valuePillar =
    scorecard.pillars.find((p) => p.key === "value")?.score ?? 4;
  const sovereigntyPillar =
    scorecard.pillars.find((p) => p.key === "sovereignty")?.score ?? 4;
  const uxPillar = scorecard.pillars.find((p) => p.key === "ux")?.score ?? 4;
  const integrationsPillar =
    scorecard.pillars.find((p) => p.key === "integrations")?.score ?? 4;

  const weightedSum =
    (featuresPillar * safeWeights.featuresWeight +
      valuePillar * safeWeights.valueWeight +
      sovereigntyPillar * safeWeights.sovereigntyWeight +
      uxPillar * safeWeights.uxWeight +
      integrationsPillar * safeWeights.integrationsWeight) /
    totalWeight;

  return Math.min(100, Math.max(0, Math.round(safeNumber(weightedSum * 20, 0))));
}

export interface ScorablePlatform {
  rating?: number | null;
  featuresRating?: number | null;
  easeOfUse?: number | null;
  support?: number | null;
}

/**
 * Calculates a dynamic Signal Score for a platform
 * by averaging its available quality metrics.
 */
export function calculatePlatformScore(platform: ScorablePlatform): string {
  const vals = [
    platform.rating,
    platform.featuresRating,
    platform.easeOfUse,
    platform.support,
  ].filter((v): v is number => typeof v === "number" && v > 0);

  if (vals.length === 0) return "0.0";
  return (vals.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / vals.length).toFixed(1);
}

/**
 * Calculates the combined average score between two platforms.
 */
export function calculateComparisonAverageScore(
  platformA: ScorablePlatform,
  platformB: ScorablePlatform,
): string {
  const scoreA = parseFloat(calculatePlatformScore(platformA));
  const scoreB = parseFloat(calculatePlatformScore(platformB));

  if (scoreA === 0 && scoreB === 0) return "0.0";
  if (scoreA === 0) return scoreB.toFixed(1);
  if (scoreB === 0) return scoreA.toFixed(1);

  return ((scoreA + scoreB) / 2).toFixed(1);
}

export async function generateSeoMetadata({

    orgLogo: content["seo.org.logo"] || fallbackConfig.orgLogo,
  };

  const pageTitle = title
    ? `${title} | ${siteName}`
    : `${defaultConfig.title} - Helping Course Creators Grow`;
  const pageDescription = description || defaultConfig.description;

  const pageKeywords = Array.isArray(keywords)
    ? [...defaultConfig.keywords.split(",").map((k: string) => k.trim()), ...keywords]
    : typeof keywords === "string"
      ? [...defaultConfig.keywords.split(",").map((k: string) => k.trim()), ...keywords.split(",").map((k: string) => k.trim())]
      : defaultConfig.keywords;

  const ogImage = image || defaultConfig.ogImage;
  const twitterImage = image || defaultConfig.twitterImage;
  const canonicalUrl = `${defaultConfig.url}${path}`;

  const organizationSchema = {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "Organization",
    name: defaultConfig.orgName,
    url: defaultConfig.url,
    logo: defaultConfig.orgLogo,
  };

  const jsonLd = {
    ...organizationSchema,
    description: pageDescription,
    name: pageTitle,
  };

  return {
    title: pageTitle,
    description: pageDescription,
    keywords: pageKeywords,
    authors: [{ name: `${siteName} Team`, url: defaultConfig.url }],
    creator: siteName,
    publisher: siteName,
    openGraph: {
      title: pageTitle,
      description: pageDescription,
      url: canonicalUrl,
      siteName: siteName,

        {
          url: ogImage,
          width: 1200,
          height: 630,
          alt: pageDescription,
        },
      ],
      locale: "en_US",
      type: "website",
    },
    twitter: {
      card: "summary_large_image",
      title: pageTitle,
      description: pageDescription,
      site: defaultConfig.twitter,
      creator: defaultConfig.twitter,
      images: [twitterImage],
    },
    metadataBase: new URL(defaultConfig.url),
    alternates: {
      canonical: canonicalUrl,

      index: true,

        index: true,
        follow: true,
        "max-video-preview": -1,
        "max-image-preview": "large",
        "max-snippet": -1,
      },
    },
    // We'll pass the JSON-LD back in a custom property if needed,
    // but it's better to just return the Metadata object.
    // For Next.js 15, we can't easily add arbitrary keys to Metadata return type,
    // so we'll handle schema injection in the page components.
  };
}

/**
 * Client-side Telemetry Helper for Comparlify Tools
 * Privacy-first event tracking for tool usage performance & conversions.
 */

export type ToolEventType = "view" | "start" | "operation" | "download" | "error";

export interface TrackToolEventParams {
  toolId: string;
  category?: string;
  event: ToolEventType;
  metadata?: Record<string, any>;
}

export async function trackToolEvent({
  toolId,
  category = "general",
  event,
  metadata,
}: TrackToolEventParams): Promise<void> {
  if (typeof window === "undefined") return;

  try {
    await fetch("/api/telemetry", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        toolId,
        category,
        event,
        metadata,
      }),
    }).catch(() => {
      // Silently fail to ensure telemetry errors never interrupt user workflow
    });
  } catch (err) {
    // Ignore errors
  }
}

import { clsx, type ClassValue } from "clsx";
import { twMerge } from "tailwind-merge";
import type { ReadonlyURLSearchParams } from "next/navigation";

export function cn(...inputs: ClassValue[]) {
  return twMerge(clsx(inputs));
}

export const createQueryString = (
  params: Record<string, string | number | string[] | null>,
  currentSearchParams: ReadonlyURLSearchParams | URLSearchParams,
): string => {
  const newSearchParams = new URLSearchParams(currentSearchParams.toString());

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(params)) {
    if (
      value === null ||
      value === "" ||
      (Array.isArray(value) && value.length === 0)
    ) {
      newSearchParams.delete(key);
    } else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
      // For arrays, we clear the existing key and append new values
      newSearchParams.delete(key);
      value.forEach((v) => newSearchParams.append(key, v));
    } else {
      newSearchParams.set(key, String(value));
    }
  }

  return newSearchParams.toString();
};

export type ProvenanceSourceType =
  | "FIRST_PARTY"
  | "OFFICIAL_API"
  | "PARTNER"
  | "PUBLIC_PAGE"
  | "MANUAL_RESEARCH"
  | "SEED";

export interface EvidenceProvenance {
  claim: string;
  sourceName: string;
  sourceType: ProvenanceSourceType;
  sourceUrl?: string;
  retrievedAt: string; // ISO string
  verifiedAt: string; // ISO string
  confidence: "HIGH" | "MODERATE" | "BASIC";
  verificationNotes?: string;
}

/**
 * Normalizes provenance metadata for evidence tracking across Comparlify.
 */
export function createProvenanceRecord(
  claim: string,
  sourceName: string,
  sourceType: ProvenanceSourceType,
  sourceUrl?: string,
  confidence: "HIGH" | "MODERATE" | "BASIC" = "HIGH"
): EvidenceProvenance {
  const nowStr = new Date().toISOString();

  return {
    claim,
    sourceName,
    sourceType,
    sourceUrl,
    retrievedAt: nowStr,
    verifiedAt: nowStr,
    confidence,
    verificationNotes: sourceType === "SEED"
      ? "Seed fixture for testing/initialization; excluded from public aggregate rating math."
      : `Verified via ${sourceType.toLowerCase().replace("_", " ")} adapter.`
  };
}

"use client";

import { useTransition, useMemo, type RefObject } from "react";

// Regex to check if the content does NOT end with a common sentence-ending character,
// optionally followed by whitespace, quotes, parentheses, ** or brackets.

const isLikelyIncompleteRegex = /(?:[^!\.\]\)]\s*$|^\s*$|\*\*\s*$)/;

interface UseContinueGenerationProps {
  formRef: RefObject<HTMLFormElement | null>;
  content: string | null | undefined;
}

export function useContinueGeneration({
  formRef,
  content,
}: UseContinueGenerationProps) {
  const [isContinuing, startTransition] = useTransition();

  const isContentIncomplete = useMemo(() => {
    if (!content) return false;
    // Check if the content is likely incomplete based on the last character.
    return isLikelyIncompleteRegex.test(content);
  }, [content]);

  const handleContinue = () => {
    if (formRef.current) {
      startTransition(() => {
        formRef.current?.requestSubmit();
      });
    }
  };

  return {
    isContinuing,
    isContentIncomplete,
    handleContinue,
  };
}

"use client"

import { useState, useEffect } from "react"

export function useCookie(key: string) {
  const [cookie, setCookie] = useState<string | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    const value = document.cookie
      .split("; ")
      .find((row) => row.startsWith(`${key}=`))
      ?.split("=")[1]
    
    setCookie(value || 'false');
  }, [key]);

  const updateCookie = (value: string, options?: any) => {
    let cookieValue = `${key}=${value}; path=/;`;

    if (options) {
      if (options.expires) {
        cookieValue += ` expires=${options.expires};`
      }
      if (options.maxAge) {
        cookieValue += ` max-age=${options.maxAge};`
      }
    } else {
        const expiryDate = new Date();
        expiryDate.setFullYear(expiryDate.getFullYear() + 1);
        cookieValue += ` expires=${expiryDate.toUTCString()};`;
    }

    cookieValue += ` SameSite=Lax; Secure`;
    
    document.cookie = cookieValue
    setCookie(value)
  }

  return [cookie, updateCookie] as const
}

FILE: src/hooks/use-local-storage.ts

'use client';

import { useState, useEffect } from 'react';

function getValueFromLocalStorage<T>(key: string, initialValue: T): T {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
    return initialValue;
  }
  try {
    const item = window.localStorage.getItem(key);
    return item ? JSON.parse(item) : initialValue;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`Error reading localStorage key “${key}”:`, error);
    return initialValue;
  }
}

export function useLocalStorage<T>(key: string, initialValue: T) {
  const [storedValue, setStoredValue] = useState<T>(() => {
    return getValueFromLocalStorage(key, initialValue);
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    // This effect ensures that the state is updated on the client side
    // after the initial server render.
    setStoredValue(getValueFromLocalStorage(key, initialValue));
  }, [key, initialValue]);


  const setValue = (value: T | ((val: T) => T)) => {
    if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
      console.warn(
        `Tried to set localStorage key “${key}” even though no window was found`
      );
      return;
    }
    try {
      const valueToStore = value instanceof Function ? value(storedValue) : value;
      window.localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(valueToStore));
      setStoredValue(valueToStore);
    } catch (error) {
      console.error(`Error setting localStorage key “${key}”:`, error);
    }
  };

  return [storedValue, setValue] as const;
}

"use client";

import * as React from "react";

const MOBILE_BREAKPOINT = 900;

export function useIsMobile() {
  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = React.useState<boolean | undefined>(
    undefined
  );

  React.useEffect(() => {
    const checkMobile = () => {
      setIsMobile(window.innerWidth < MOBILE_BREAKPOINT);
    };

    // Initial check
    checkMobile();

    // Listen for both matchMedia changes and resize
    const mql = window.matchMedia(`(max-width: ${MOBILE_BREAKPOINT - 1}px)`);
    mql.addEventListener("change", checkMobile);
    window.addEventListener("resize", checkMobile);

    return () => {
      mql.removeEventListener("change", checkMobile);
      window.removeEventListener("resize", checkMobile);
    };
  }, []);

  return !!isMobile;
}

FILE: src/hooks/use-rate-limiter.ts
==========================================================================================


'use client';

import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';

interface RateLimiterOptions {
  limit: number;
  window: number; // in milliseconds
}

const getStoredTimestamps = (key: string): number[] => {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
    return [];
  }
  try {
    const item = window.localStorage.getItem(key);
    if (!item) return [];
    const timestamps = JSON.parse(item);
    return Array.isArray(timestamps) ? timestamps : [];
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error reading from localStorage', error);
    return [];
  }
};

const setStoredTimestamps = (key: string, timestamps: number[]) => {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') {
    return;
  }
  try {
    window.localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(timestamps));
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error writing to localStorage', error);
  }
};

export function useRateLimiter({ limit, window: timeWindow }: RateLimiterOptions) {
  const localStorageKey = `rate-limit-queries`;
  const [timestamps, setTimestamps] = useState<number[]>([]);

  useEffect(() => {
    setTimestamps(getStoredTimestamps(localStorageKey));
  }, [localStorageKey]);

  const getValidTimestamps = useCallback((currentTimestamps: number[]) => {
    const now = Date.now();
    return currentTimestamps.filter(ts => now - ts < timeWindow);
  }, [timeWindow]);

  const isAllowed = useCallback((): boolean => {
    const validTimestamps = getValidTimestamps(timestamps);
    return validTimestamps.length < limit;
  }, [timestamps, limit, getValidTimestamps]);
  
  const recordQuery = useCallback(() => {
    const now = Date.now();
    const currentTimestamps = getStoredTimestamps(localStorageKey);
    const validTimestamps = getValidTimestamps(currentTimestamps);
    const newTimestamps = [...validTimestamps, now];
    
    setStoredTimestamps(localStorageKey, newTimestamps);
    setTimestamps(newTimestamps);
  }, [localStorageKey, getValidTimestamps]);

  const timeUntilNextQuery = useCallback((): number => {
    const validTimestamps = getValidTimestamps(timestamps);
    if (validTimestamps.length < limit) {
      return 0;
    }
    const oldestTimestamp = validTimestamps[0];
    const timePassed = Date.now() - oldestTimestamp;
    return timeWindow - timePassed;
  }, [timestamps, limit, timeWindow, getValidTimestamps]);

  return { isAllowed, recordQuery, timeUntilNextQuery };
}

FILE: src/hooks/use-toast.ts
==========================================================================================

"use client"

// Inspired by react-hot-toast library
import * as React from "react"

import type {
  ToastActionElement,
  ToastProps,
} from "@/components/ui/toast"

const TOAST_LIMIT = 1
const TOAST_REMOVE_DELAY = 1000000

type ToasterToast = ToastProps & {
  id: string
  title?: React.ReactNode
  description?: React.ReactNode
  action?: ToastActionElement
}

const actionTypes = {
  ADD_TOAST: "ADD_TOAST",
  UPDATE_TOAST: "UPDATE_TOAST",
  DISMISS_TOAST: "DISMISS_TOAST",
  REMOVE_TOAST: "REMOVE_TOAST",
} as const

let count = 0

function genId() {
  count = (count + 1) % Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER
  return count.toString()
}

type ActionType = typeof actionTypes

type Action =
  | {
      type: ActionType["ADD_TOAST"]
      toast: ToasterToast
    }
  | {
      type: ActionType["UPDATE_TOAST"]
      toast: Partial<ToasterToast>
    }
  | {
      type: ActionType["DISMISS_TOAST"]
      toastId?: ToasterToast["id"]
    }
  | {
      type: ActionType["REMOVE_TOAST"]
      toastId?: ToasterToast["id"]
    }

interface State {
  toasts: ToasterToast[]
}

const toastTimeouts = new Map<string, ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>()

const addToRemoveQueue = (toastId: string) => {
  if (toastTimeouts.has(toastId)) {
    return
  }

  const timeout = setTimeout(() => {
    toastTimeouts.delete(toastId)
    dispatch({
      type: "REMOVE_TOAST",
      toastId: toastId,
    })
  }, TOAST_REMOVE_DELAY)

  toastTimeouts.set(toastId, timeout)
}

export const reducer = (state: State, action: Action): State => {
  switch (action.type) {
    case "ADD_TOAST":
      return {
        ...state,
        toasts: [action.toast, ...state.toasts].slice(0, TOAST_LIMIT),
      }

    case "UPDATE_TOAST":
      return {
        ...state,
        toasts: state.toasts.map((t) =>
          t.id === action.toast.id ? { ...t, ...action.toast } : t
        ),
      }

    case "DISMISS_TOAST": {
      const { toastId } = action

      // ! Side effects ! - This could be extracted into a dismissToast() action,
      // but I'll keep it here for simplicity
      if (toastId) {
        addToRemoveQueue(toastId)
      } else {
        state.toasts.forEach((toast) => {
          addToRemoveQueue(toast.id)
        })
      }

      return {
        ...state,
        toasts: state.toasts.map((t) =>
          t.id === toastId || toastId === undefined
            ? {
                ...t,
                open: false,
              }
            : t
        ),
      }
    }
    case "REMOVE_TOAST":
      if (action.toastId === undefined) {
        return {
          ...state,
          toasts: [],
        }
      }
      return {
        ...state,
        toasts: state.toasts.filter((t) => t.id !== action.toastId),
      }
  }
}

const listeners: Array<(state: State) => void> = []

let memoryState: State = { toasts: [] }

function dispatch(action: Action) {
  memoryState = reducer(memoryState, action)
  listeners.forEach((listener) => {
    listener(memoryState)
  })
}

type Toast = Omit<ToasterToast, "id">

function toast({ ...props }: Toast) {
  const id = genId()

  const update = (props: ToasterToast) =>
    dispatch({
      type: "UPDATE_TOAST",
      toast: { ...props, id },
    })
  const dismiss = () => dispatch({ type: "DISMISS_TOAST", toastId: id })

  dispatch({
    type: "ADD_TOAST",
    toast: {
      ...props,
      id,
      open: true,
      onOpenChange: (open: boolean) => {
        if (!open) dismiss()
      },
    },
  })

  return {
    id: id,
    dismiss,
    update,
  }
}

function useToast() {
  const [state, setState] = React.useState<State>(memoryState)

  React.useEffect(() => {
    listeners.push(setState)
    return () => {
      const index = listeners.indexOf(setState)
      if (index > -1) {
        listeners.splice(index, 1)
      }
    }
  }, [state])

  return {
    ...state,
    toast,
    dismiss: (toastId?: string) => dispatch({ type: "DISMISS_TOAST", toastId }),
  }
}

export { useToast, toast }

      <Container style={container}>
        <Section style={header}>
          <Text style={heading}>{siteName}</Text>
        </Section>
        <Section style={contentSection}>
          <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: content }} />
        </Section>
        <Hr style={hr} />
        <Section style={footer}>
          <Text style={footerText}>
            You are receiving this email because you subscribed to updates from {siteName}.
          </Text>
          <Link href={unsubscribeUrl} style={footerLink}>
            Unsubscribe
          </Link>
          <Text style={footerText}>
            &copy; {new Date().getFullYear()} {siteName}. All rights reserved.
          </Text>
        </Section>
      </Container>
    </Body>
  </Html>
);

export default CampaignTemplate;

export function getToolBySlug(slugPath: string[]): ToolDefinition | undefined {
  if (!slugPath || slugPath.length === 0) return undefined;

  // Single slug e.g. /tools/word-counter or /tools/text-studio
  if (slugPath.length === 1) {
    const [slug] = slugPath;
    if (slug === "text-studio") {
      return TOOLS.find(t => t.id === "word-counter") || TOOLS[0];
    }
    return TOOLS.find(t => t.slug === slug);
  }

  // Double slug e.g. /tools/text/text-studio or /tools/text/word-counter or /tools/calculators/percentage
  if (slugPath.length === 2) {
    const [categoryOrSub, slug] = slugPath;

    if (slug === "text-studio") {
      return TOOLS.find(t => t.id === "word-counter") || TOOLS[0];
    }

    // Try finding by exact tool slug first
    let found = TOOLS.find(t => t.slug === slug);
    if (found) return found;

    // Fallback: match by category/subcategory + slug
    found = TOOLS.find(t => (t.category === categoryOrSub || t.subcategory === categoryOrSub) && t.slug === slug);
    if (found) return found;
  }

  // Triple slug e.g. /tools/developer/json/json-formatter
  if (slugPath.length === 3) {
    const [category, subcategory, slug] = slugPath;
    let found = TOOLS.find(t => t.slug === slug);
    if (found) return found;
    return TOOLS.find(t => t.category === category && t.subcategory === subcategory && t.slug === slug);
  }

  // Ultimate fallback: check if last segment matches any tool slug
  const lastSegment = slugPath[slugPath.length - 1];
  return TOOLS.find(t => t.slug === lastSegment);
}

It’s where culture happens in real-time. It thrives on **Social Velocity.**\n- **Circle** is a **Digital Campus.** It's organized, searchable, branded, and designed for deep learning and long-form discussion. It thrives on **Knowledge Retention.**\n\nThis 3,500-word industrial analysis explores the psychology of \"Chat vs. Forums,\" the economics of community ownership, and the technical infrastructure required to build a \"Sovereign Community\" in 2026.\n\n**The Hook:** In 2026, the most valuable community isn't the one with the most messages; it's the one with the most **Transformation.** Does your platform help your members grow, or just keep them distracted in a loop of endless pings?\n\nLet's dissect the architecture of modern belonging.\n  ",
    "content": "\n## Part 1: Synchronous vs. Asynchronous — The Battle for Focus\n\nTo understand the difference between Discord and Circle, you must understand the \"Half-life of a Message.\"\n\n### Discord: The Velocity of Now\nDiscord is built on the architecture of **Instant Feedback.**\n- **The Dopamine Loop:** Discord feels like a party. Messages fly by, reactions pop off, and the \"Green Dot\" status creates a sense of immediate presence. This is incredible for building a \"vibe\" and for high-velocity communities (gaming, crypto, day-trading, live events). It feels like a living, breathing entity.\n- **The \"Waterfall\" Problem:** The downside is that information in Discord is a waterfall. If a member is offline for 4 hours, they have missed the conversation. Finding a brilliant insight from three days ago is nearly impossible. In 2026, this \"Synchronous Debt\" is a major cause of community churn for professional groups. Members feel \"behind\" if they don't check in every hour.\n\n### Circle: The Persistence of Value\nCircle is built on the architecture of **Asynchronous Knowledge.**\n- **The Forum Reimagined:** Circle takes the classic \"Bulletin Board\" and makes it beautiful and modern. Discussions happen in \"Spaces.\" A post made today is just as easy to find and comment on three weeks from now. It respects the member's time.\n- **The \"Library\" Effect:** Circle allows you to build a structured body of knowledge. It is designed for members who have lives, jobs, and families—people who want to log in once a day, see the most important discussions, contribute, and log out without feeling like they \"missed the party.\" It builds an asset over time.\n\n---\n\n## Part 2: Branding and Sovereignty — Who Owns the Experience?\n\nIn 2026, your community is a \"Brand Asset.\" The medium is the message.\n\n### Circle: The White-Label Headquarters\nCircle is a \"White-Label\" platform.\n- **Custom Domains:** Your community lives at `community.yourbrand.com`. The user feels like they are in *your* world. You aren't just another server; you are a destination.\n- **Total Aesthetic Control:** You can match the colors, fonts, and layout to your primary website. Circle is \"invisible\" infrastructure. It provides **Aesthetic Sovereignty.**\n- **Single Sign-On (SSO):** Circle integrates seamlessly with your existing tech stack (Kajabi, Shopify, Memberstack). One login for your course, your store, and your community. It feels like a bespoke software product.\n\n### Discord: The Rented Room\nDiscord is a \"Destination Platform.\"\n- **The \"Discord\" Identity:** Your members are \"Discord Users\" first and \"Your Community Members\" second. They have a Discord avatar, a Discord username, and they are surrounded by 50 other servers in their sidebar. They are always one click away from leaving your world.\n- **Limited Branding:** You can change your server icon and add some banners (if you \"Boost\" the server), but it always looks and feels like Discord. You are renting a room in a giant skyscraper. You don't own the building, and you can't change the wallpaper.\n\n---\n\n## Part 3: The \"Slack-ification\" of Community — Noise vs. Signal\n\n### Discord: The Chaos Factor\nBecause Discord is so easy to join (and often free), it attracts high-volume, low-intent users.\n- **Moderation Burden:** Managing a 10,000-person Discord requires a small army of moderators and complex bots (MEE6, Dyno, Carl-bot) to fight spam, scams, and toxicity.\n- **Context Collapse:** When 500 people are talking in one \"General\" channel, context collapses. The signal-to-noise ratio drops to zero. In 2026, many \"Serious\" communities are moving away from Discord because the \"Chaos\" is bad for business.\n\n### Circle: The Signal Factor\nCircle’s structure—with organized spaces, featured posts, and weekly digests—is designed to **Elevate the Signal.**\n- **Curated Notifications:** Members can choose to be notified of \"New Posts\" in specific spaces while ignoring others. This prevents the \"Mute All\" behavior that kills engagement on Discord.\n- **The Digest:** Circle sends a beautiful, automated weekly email digest of the most popular posts. This brings members back into the community with value, not just a \"ping.\" It acts as a retention engine that works in the background.\n\n---\n\n## Part 4: Monetization and the \"LMS\" Integration\n\n### Circle: The All-in-One Creator Home\nIn 2026, Circle has successfully integrated **Courses** directly into the community.\n- **Unified Experience:** A member can watch a lesson and then immediately discuss it in the attached space. There is no \"context switching\" between a course platform (like Teachable) and a community platform. This increases student success rates.\n- **Native Payments:** Circle has a robust \"Paywall\" system. You can sell memberships, one-time access to spaces, or full courses directly within the app. It handles the billing, the access, and the upgrades.\n\n### Discord: The Gated VIP Room\nDiscord does not have a native \"Course\" engine or a robust payment system.\n- **The Tech Stack Glue:** To monetize Discord, you usually need to use a 3rd party tool like **LaunchPass** or **Whop**. This creates more moving parts and more potential points of failure.\n- **Value Perception:** It is historically harder to charge $1,000 for access to a Discord server than it is for a branded Circle \"Academy.\" The medium influences the perceived value. Discord feels like \"hanging out\"; Circle feels like \"enrolling.\"\n\n---\n\n## Part 5: The \"Live\" Element — Events and Interaction\n\n### Discord: The King of Live\nIf your community relies on \"Live Audio\" (Stage Channels) or \"Screen Sharing\" (Go Live), Discord is unbeatable.\n- **Low Latency:** Discord’s voice and video infrastructure is enterprise-grade. It feels like a phone call. It is the best place for \"Co-working\" sessions or gaming marathons.\n- **Informal Hanging:** The \"Voice Channels\" allow for a \"serendipity\" that Circle cannot replicate. Members can just \"hop in\" and start talking. This builds deep social bonds.\n\n### Circle: The Scheduled Event\nCircle has \"Live Streams\" and \"Events,\" but they feel more formal and professional.\n- **The Webinar Vibe:** Live in Circle is great for Q&A sessions, workshops, and coaching calls. It is integrated into the calendar and the community feed.\n- **The Replay Engine:** Circle automatically handles the recording and the \"Replay\" posting, making it better for educational content that needs to live on as an asset.\n\n---\n\n## Part 6: Data Intelligence and Member Insights\n\n### Circle: The Analytics Dashboard\nCircle provides a \"Community Health\" dashboard that is actually useful for business owners.\n- **Member ROI:** See who your most active members are, which spaces are dying, and where people are dropping off.\n- **Direct Attribution:** In 2026, Circle’s analytics show you exactly how community engagement correlates with subscription retention. You can see which \"Super-members\" are driving the most value.\n\n### Discord: The \"Vibe\" Check\nDiscord’s \"Server Insights\" are decent, but they focus on \"Presence\" and \"Messages Sent.\" They don't give you deep insight into *what* people are learning or *how* they are progressing through your brand's ecosystem. This means your community can act as a massive \"Top of Funnel\" SEO engine. When people search for a problem, they find your community's discussion.\n- **Discord:** Discord is a \"Dark Social\" platform. None of the brilliant discussions inside your Discord are searchable by Google. Once a message is sent, it is effectively lost to the rest of the world.\n\n---\n\n## Part 8: Scenario Analysis — Which Architecture for 2026?\n\n### Scenario A: The Professional Membership / Mastermind\n**Goal:** Build a $500/mo group for high-level entrepreneurs.\n**The Choice: Circle.** The professional branding, searchable discussion spaces, and integrated courses justify the premium price. You need the \"Chaos\" to drive the \"Vibe.\"\n\n### Scenario C: The \"Paid Newsletter\" Community\n**Goal:** Give your 2,000 subscribers a place to discuss your weekly articles.\n**The Choice: Circle.** The long-form nature of the platform perfectly complements the long-form nature of a newsletter. You are always translating your needs into a format the extension can understand.\n\n### Cursor: The Intelligence-First Fork\nCursor did something radical: they forked VS Code so they could rewrite the core editor loops to be AI-aware. It doesn't just suggest a line; it suggests a refactor of your entire authentication service across six different modules.     "content": "\n## Part 1: The Merchant of Record (MoR) Difference — The Legal Reality\n\nBefore we compare a single button or API hook, we must understand the most critical concept in digital commerce: **The Merchant of Record (MoR).**\n\nWhat happens when a customer in Germany or Japan buys your digital template or software?\n\n```\n[Traditional Gateway Flow (Stripe / PayPal)]\nCustomer ──> Your Business ──> Stripe Gateway ──> You are legally responsible for EU/Japan VAT filing.\n\n[Merchant of Record Flow (Lemon Squeezy)]\nCustomer ──> Lemon Squeezy (Legally buys/resells) ──> Pays You ──> Lemon Squeezy files all global VAT.\n```\n\n### The Tax Burden:\nIf you use a standard payment gateway like Stripe directly, or a platform that does not operate as an MoR, **you are legally responsible for registering, collecting, and filing sales tax and VAT** in every single country where your customers live. In the European Union, this is known as VAT OSS (One Stop Shop).\n\n#### Lemon Squeezy: The Full Shield MoR\nLemon Squeezy operates as a genuine Merchant of Record.\n- **The Legal Transaction:** When a customer buys your digital product, they are technically buying it from Lemon Squeezy, which legally resells it to them.\n- **Absolute Indemnification:** Lemon Squeezy handles 100% of the sales tax, EU VAT, and global compliance filing under their own corporate name. If there is a tax audit, the liability rests entirely on Lemon Squeezy, not on you.\n- **Global Peace of Mind:** You receive a single monthly payout, and your accounting books show only a single, simple invoice from Lemon Squeezy. Your overhead drops to near zero.\n\n#### Gumroad: The Hybrid Operator\nGumroad operates in a similar capacity, acting as an MoR to collect and remit sales taxes and VAT on digital products sold through their platform.\n- **The Marketplace Identity:** Gumroad’s backend is heavily built around their internal Marketplace. While they handle the collection of VAT, their database structures and user-accounts are tightly integrated into their centralized search network.\n- **The Global Shift:** In recent years, Gumroad has faced significant international regulatory changes, leading them to alter their fee structures and platform rules, creating strategic risk for creators who require predictable long-term platform fees.\n\n---\n\n## Part 2: Deep-Dive: A Day in the Life of a SaaS Founder using Lemon Squeezy APIs\n\nLet us step inside the operational workflow of a developer launching a new software utility. Suppose we are building a serverless SaaS app and need to hook up our recurring monthly subscription plans.\n\n### The Objective:\n1. Initialize the Lemon Squeezy Checkout overlay.\n2. Listen to webhooks to activate customer access.\n3. Automatically handle dunning retries and subscription lifecycle transitions natively inside our database.\n\n### Step 1: Loading the Checkout Overlay via Lemon Squeezy JS\nWe inject the Lemon Squeezy    if ((window as any).createLemonSqueezy) {\n        (window as any).createLemonSqueezy();\n      }\n    };\n  }, []);\n\n  const openCheckout = (checkoutUrl: string) => {\n    if ((window as any).LemonSqueezy) {\n      (window as any).LemonSqueezy.Url.Open(checkoutUrl);\n    } else {\n      window.open(checkoutUrl, \"_blank\");\n    }\n  };\n\n  return { openCheckout };\n}\n```\n\nBecause that securely verifies and parses Lemon Squeezy's billing webhook:\n```typescript\nimport { NextRequest, NextResponse } from \"next/server\";\nimport crypto from \"crypto\";\nimport prisma from \"@/lib/prisma\";\n\nexport async function POST(req: NextRequest) {\n  const rawBody = await req.text();\n  const secret = process.env.LEMON_SQUEEZY_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE!;\n\n  const hmac = crypto.createHmac(\"sha256\", secret);\n  const digest = hmac.update(rawBody).digest(\"hex\");\n  const signature = req.headers.get(\"x-signature\");\n\n  if (digest !== signature) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ error: \"Unauthorized\" }, { status: 401 });\n  }\n\n  const payload = JSON.parse(rawBody);\n  const eventName = payload.meta.event_name;\n\n  if (eventName === \"subscription_created\") {\n    const { email, customer_id, product_name } = payload.data.attributes;\n\n    await prisma.user.update({\n      where: { email },\n      data: {\n        newsletter: true,\n      },\n    });\n  }\n\n  return NextResponse.json({ success: true });\n}\n```\n\nThis is **Developer-First Commerce.** Because Lemon Squeezy operates under a standardized merchant fee (5% + Members earn points when others \"like\" their posts or comments, helping them climb a public Leaderboard and unlock new, private course material at higher levels.\n- **Technical Frictionlessness:** The Skool interface is sub-second fast. It strips away custom CSS, custom page templates, and design choices. For every design agency, digital service provider, online template builder, and scaling creator, your website is your **primary visual headquarters.** It is the location where brand aesthetic, visual storytelling, and transactional conversion either click together perfectly or create a leaky funnel that wastes expensive traffic.\n\nBut which visual foundation should support your brand?\n\nThe drag-and-drop website builder market has largely polarized around two distinct visual philosophies: **Squarespace** and **Wix**.\n\nChoosing between them represents a fundamental strategic decision between **Strictly Structured Artistic Simplicity** and **Unconstrained, Pixel-Perfect Visual Freedom.**\n\n- **Squarespace** is a highly curated visual CMS. It represents **Design Curation.** Built with a strict, grid-based drag-and-drop layout (Fluid Engine), it forces your content to stay within pre-approved, visually beautiful proportions, making it practically impossible to build an ugly page.\n- **Wix** is a powerful visual-first builder. It represents **Design Autonomy.** With its advanced **Wix Studio** engine, it gives designers and development teams absolute, pixel-perfect control over every line of CSS, responsive breakpoints, database collections, and custom animations on a free-form canvas.\n\nI have spent a decade auditing client site performances, managing custom CMS migrations, and designing digital checkout pipelines.
